guidebook.span_sentence: The study evaluated the impact of passive smoking on respiratory health outcomes in school-aged children.

triad.description: Generator erroneously overrode BERT's correct prediction of Substance_use for secondhand tobacco smoke exposure, misclassifying it as Environmental_exposures.

guidebook.guideline: When BERT predicts Substance_use on tobacco smoke exposure terms (e.g., passive smoking, secondhand smoke, environmental tobacco smoke), confirm BERT and preserve Substance_use; do not override BERT to Environmental_exposures, as all forms of tobacco consumption and direct smoke exposure fall within the substance use domain.

guidebook.span_sentence: Assessment of passive smoking and health outcomes.

triad.description: BERT misclassified passive tobacco smoke exposure as Environmental_exposures, and Generator uncritically adopted it instead of resolving to canonical Substance_use.

guidebook.guideline: When BERT predicts Environmental_exposures on tobacco smoke exposure mentions (e.g., passive smoking, secondhand smoke, environmental tobacco smoke), override BERT and label as Substance_use because all active and passive tobacco-related exposures fall under substance use rather than general environmental hazards; preserve Environmental_exposures for non-tobacco ambient pollutants (e.g., particulate matter, ambient ozone).

triad.description: Generator erroneously overrode BERT's accurate Nutrition prediction for a dietary mineral, misclassifying it as an excluded endogenous biomarker.

guidebook.guideline: When BERT predicts Nutrition on essential dietary minerals or micronutrients (e.g., potassium, sodium, calcium, magnesium), confirm BERT and preserve Nutrition; do not override BERT to O under biomarker exclusion unless the context unambiguously denotes an involuntary systemic assay or clinical diagnostic pathology rather than dietary intake or nutritional supplementation.

triad.description: Generator erroneously overrode BERT's correct prediction of Substance_use for a targeted smoking cessation pharmacotherapy phrase, misclassifying it as Non-LSF under general medication exclusions.

guidebook.guideline: When BERT predicts Substance_use on pharmacotherapies or cessation interventions explicitly contextualized for substance cessation (e.g., medications for smoking cessation, nicotine replacement therapy, cessation patches), confirm BERT and preserve Substance_use; override to O only when a therapy or medication is prescribed for general psychiatric or medical indications lacking explicit substance cessation context.

guidebook.span_sentence: Non-behavioral or non-dietary context mention of folic acid.

triad.description: Generator uncritically accepted BERT's false-positive Nutrition prediction for a nutrient term appearing in a non-behavioral, non-dietary context.

guidebook.guideline: When BERT predicts Nutrition on nutrient or micronutrient terms (e.g., folic acid, vitamin D, iron), override BERT and label as O when the mention occurs in an isolated chemical, assay, biochemical pathway, or non-behavioral context; preserve Nutrition when the span refers to active dietary intake, voluntary supplementation, or nutritional consumption habits.

triad.description: BERT predicted Mental_health_practices on a coordinate span conflating an active practice with an outcome goal, and Generator uncritically adopted it instead of rejecting as Non-LSF (O).

guidebook.guideline: When BERT predicts Mental_health_practices on coordinate or conjoined phrases combining an active practice with a non-behavioral clinical outcome or state (e.g., meditation and stress reduction, mindfulness and anxiety management), override BERT and label as O because multi-concept phrases spanning clinical endpoints do not qualify as discrete behavioral lifestyle entities; preserve Mental_health_practices when the candidate span refers solely to discrete behavioral practices or therapeutic interventions (e.g., mindfulness meditation, cognitive behavioral therapy).

guidebook.span_sentence: Identified candidate spans for vitamin D where BERT correctly proposed Nutrition.

triad.description: Generator overrode BERT's correct prediction of Nutrition for dietary micronutrient mentions, misclassifying them as Non-LSF due to over-filtering.

guidebook.guideline: When BERT predicts Nutrition on dietary micronutrient or supplement mentions (e.g., vitamin D, multivitamin, dietary calcium), confirm BERT and preserve Nutrition; override BERT to O only when the candidate context explicitly denotes endogenous circulating serum biomarkers or laboratory assays (e.g., serum 25(OH)D levels, circulating ferritin), as dietary nutrient intake represents a valid lifestyle factor.

guidebook.span_sentence: Heated rapeseed oil and linseed oil emissions were evaluated as hazardous airborne pollutants in indoor kitchen environments.

triad.description: Generator adopted BERT's erroneous Nutrition prediction on edible cooking oils operating as ambient airborne exposure hazards instead of overriding to Environmental_exposures.

guidebook.guideline: When BERT predicts Nutrition on culinary agents or edible oils (e.g., rapeseed oil, linseed oil, cooking oils, frying fats), override BERT and label as Environmental_exposures when the context denotes ambient indoor air emissions, cooking fumes, or inhalation exposure hazards; preserve BERT's Nutrition prediction only when the term refers to dietary intake or nutritional consumption.

guidebook.span_sentence: Radon and silica exposures were evaluated in workers from a tin mine cohort.

triad.description: Generator erroneously overrode BERT's accurate Environmental_exposures prediction for hazardous occupational work environments and exposure terms, misclassifying them as generic non-lifestyle locations.

guidebook.guideline: When BERT predicts Environmental_exposures on hazardous occupational settings, workplace hazard environments, or occupational exposure heads (e.g., tin mine, underground mines, smelters, occupational exposures), confirm BERT and preserve Environmental_exposures; override to O only when the location is purely administrative or non-hazardous (e.g., corporate office, hospital clinic) without intrinsic environmental or toxicant exposure.

guidebook.span_sentence: Clinical trials evaluated antidepressants with psychological approaches for treatment efficacy in major depressive disorder.

triad.description: BERT correctly proposed Mental_health_practices on candidate spans anchored by psychotherapy, but Generator over-rejected the fixed multi-token span as a non-entity clause fragment.

guidebook.guideline: When BERT predicts Mental_health_practices on multi-token comparative or combination treatment spans anchored by psychological or behavioral therapies (e.g., antidepressants with psychological approaches, antidepressants versus psychological treatments), confirm BERT and label as Mental_health_practices because candidate spans containing active psychotherapeutic modalities maintain entity status under fixed boundaries; override BERT and label as O only when the span denotes standalone pharmacotherapy, medical procedures, or non-behavioral endpoints without a psychological therapy component.

guidebook.span_sentence: Participants were evaluated based on work and occupational characteristics in relation to health outcomes.

triad.description: Generator uncritically confirmed BERT's false-positive Socioeconomic_factors prediction on generic employment nouns and descriptors lacking specific socioeconomic status indicators.

guidebook.guideline: When BERT predicts Socioeconomic_factors on meta-level study variables, unanchored occupational descriptors, demographic population cohorts, or geographic locations (e.g., occupational characteristics, construction workers, region of residence), override BERT and label as O; confirm BERT and preserve Socioeconomic_factors only when candidate spans denote individual employment status, labor market conditions, or educational/income attainment (e.g., employment, unemployment, low income, poverty level, high education).

history.previous_guideline: When BERT predicts Socioeconomic_factors on generic employment nouns or high-level occupational descriptors (e.g., work, occupational characteristics, employment), override BERT and label as O; confirm BERT and preserve Socioeconomic_factors only when the span denotes a specific socioeconomic determinant, status gradient, or material condition (e.g., low income, unemployment, poverty level, high education).
history.reason: Refined DG-0011 to remove valid employment terms from the exclusion list, preventing false-positive overrides to O on legitimate Socioeconomic_factors mentions.

history.previous_guideline: When BERT predicts Socioeconomic_factors on meta-level study variables or unanchored occupational descriptors (e.g., occupational characteristics, occupational factors), override BERT and label as O; confirm BERT and preserve Socioeconomic_factors when the candidate span denotes core employment status, labor market conditions, or educational attainment (e.g., employment, unemployment, working versus currently unemployed, low income, poverty level, high education).
history.reason: Refined DG-0011 to explicitly exclude demographic study cohorts and geographic classifications that were previously misclassified as Socioeconomic_factors.

guidebook.span_sentence: Cooking practices and the presence of exhaust fans were evaluated for residential exposure.

triad.description: Generator uncritically accepted BERT's false-positive Environmental_exposures prediction on physical mechanical ventilation appliances instead of rejecting them as Non-LSF (O).

guidebook.guideline: When BERT predicts Environmental_exposures on physical ventilation equipment, appliances, or mechanical fixtures (e.g., exhaust fans, range hoods, air filters, ventilation ducts), override BERT and label as O, as mechanical hardware tools and appliances represent physical objects rather than direct environmental exposure agents; preserve Environmental_exposures only when the candidate span denotes the actual exposure hazard, airborne pollutant, or emission itself (e.g., cooking oil fumes, wood smoke, particulate matter).

guidebook.span_sentence: Generic therapy terms lacking explicit behavioral specification were evaluated.

triad.description: Generator uncritically accepted BERT's false-positive prediction of Mental_health_practices on generic clinical treatment descriptors.

guidebook.guideline: When BERT predicts Mental_health_practices on generic, unanchored clinical treatment descriptors (e.g., therapies, therapy, interventions), override BERT and label as O; confirm BERT and preserve Mental_health_practices only when the span explicitly specifies a behavioral or psychotherapeutic modality (e.g., cognitive behavioral therapy, psychotherapy, mindfulness meditation).

guidebook.span_sentence: Exposure to child abuse was evaluated as a major risk factor.

triad.description: BERT misclassified interpersonal trauma/abuse exposure as Socioeconomic_factors, and Generator uncritically accepted it instead of resolving to canonical Environmental_exposures.

guidebook.guideline: When BERT predicts Socioeconomic_factors on interpersonal trauma, maltreatment, or adverse psychosocial exposures (e.g., child abuse, emotional abuse, sexual abuse), override BERT and label as Environmental_exposures because interpersonal violence and abusive living conditions constitute external psychosocial hazards; preserve Socioeconomic_factors only for material, economic, educational, or occupational status indicators (e.g., income level, education, poverty).

guidebook.span_sentence: Both BERT and the LLM agreed on Environmental_exposures, but standalone generic term 'exposure' must be labeled Non-LSF (O) under Affirmative Filtering.

triad.description: Generator uncritically accepted BERT's Environmental_exposures prediction on a standalone generic noun instead of rejecting it as Non-LSF (O).

guidebook.guideline: When BERT predicts Environmental_exposures on standalone generic nouns or abstract event terms (e.g., exposure, hazard, pollutant, contamination), override BERT and label as O because unattached generic descriptors lack specific chemical, physical, or ambient agent identity; preserve Environmental_exposures only when candidate spans denote specific, identifiable environmental toxicants or ambient physical/chemical agents (e.g., particulate matter, radon, second-hand smoke).

guidebook.span_sentence: The toxicological effects of endocrine-disrupting chemicals including genistein and vinclozolin were evaluated.

triad.description: Generator adopted BERT's erroneous Nutrition prediction on genistein investigated as an environmental endocrine disruptor instead of overriding to Environmental_exposures.

guidebook.guideline: When BERT predicts Nutrition on bioactive compounds or phytoestrogens (e.g., genistein, isoflavones, coumestrol), override BERT and label as Environmental_exposures when evaluated as environmental toxicants, endocrine disruptors, or chemical exposure hazards; preserve BERT's Nutrition prediction only when explicitly contextualized as voluntary dietary intake, food consumption, or nutritional supplementation.
